title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a programmatic map of the rings of cycle classes A^*(X) for X smooth projective over an algebraically closed field k, one ring for each adequate equivalence relation. It is the diagrammatic counterpart of the 'Tableau des données de cycles' on p.90. It probably dates from about 1968–71, since it cites Lieberman's equivalences (Lieberman, Amer. J. Math. 1968).

(1) 'Théorie discrète' (upper box). Top: A_num, numerical equivalence. Below it: A_Z, which I read as A_τ, τ-equivalence, i.e. algebraic equivalence modulo torsion. Below that: A_alg, algebraic equivalence.
- Horizontal maps: A_alg -(≃?)-> A_{Z_ℓ-hom} (image of the integral ℓ-adic cycle map) and A_τ -(≃?)-> A_{Q_ℓ-hom}.
- Vertical maps: A_{Z_ℓ-hom} -> A_{Q_ℓ-hom}, plus A_{Q_ℓ-hom} -> A_num via the arrow '? Z', probably '⊗Q ≃?'.
- The questions asked:
  - Is algebraic equivalence the same as ℓ-adic homological equivalence, integrally and rationally?
  - Is homological equivalence numerical equivalence rationally? This is standard conjecture D.
  - Brace 'groupe libre de type fini?': are A_num and A_τ free of finite type?
  - Brace 'groupe fini?': is the kernel of A_alg -> A_τ, the torsion of cycles modulo algebraic equivalence, finite?
- A third column, apparently a second ℓ-adic theory (independence of ℓ), is crossed out.
- A circled note ('HC', possibly 'AH') near A_{Z_ℓ-hom} is linked to 'C-ex.?/car. 0, au moins en théorie transcendante'. This most likely records that integral (torsion) cohomology classes need not be algebraic. That is the Atiyah–Hirzebruch counterexample (1962) to the integral Hodge conjecture, known in characteristic 0 for Betti cohomology.

(2) 'Théorie continue' (lower box). It contains A_lin -> A_alb -> A_pic, with each arrow marked '?', and all arrows declared surjective ('flèches toutes surjectives').
- A_lin is rational (linear) equivalence, i.e. the Chow ring.
- A_alb and A_pic are intermediate equivalences: kill the kernel of an Albanese-type map, respectively a Picard-type map, on cycles algebraically equivalent to 0.
- The arrow A_pic -> A_alg is braced 'V.A.?'. The question is whether the kernel (cycles algebraically equivalent to zero, modulo the Pic-type equivalence) is an abelian variety, by analogy with Pic^0 = ker(Pic -> NS) for divisors. This is the problem of the algebraic representative / regular homomorphisms (Samuel 1960, later Murre).

(3) Left column, K-theory. CK = K_0 of the Chow ring side, with surjections
- CK -> G_alg K (graded for an algebraic filtration, e.g. γ or coniveau) -> G_top K (graded for the topological filtration).
- These are labelled 'flèches qui sont des isomorphismes de torsion': kernel and cokernel are torsion. This is SGA 6 Riemann–Roch (ch: K⊗Q ≅ CH⊗Q; CH^p -> Gr^p_top K has kernel killed by (p-1)!).
- CK also maps onto A_lin.
- A dashed arrow with '?' runs from G_top K toward A_{Z_ℓ-hom}. It asks for an integral comparison between topological-filtration graded K-theory and integral ℓ-adic cycle classes, an algebraic analogue of Atiyah–Hirzebruch.

(4) Bottom right: 'Autres équivalences: l'équivalence algébrique r[?] et les équivalences de Weil[?], wh et W, définies par Lieberman' — further relations to be placed in the lattice.
errors: No outright mathematical errors; the page is a list of questions. Several '≃?' have since been answered negatively: A_alg -> A_{Z_ℓ-hom} and A_τ -> A_{Q_ℓ-hom} are not isomorphisms in general (Griffiths 1969: the Griffiths group can be non-torsion).

'Groupe fini?' for the torsion in cycles modulo algebraic equivalence: the answer is no in general. Schoen showed the torsion in the Griffiths group can be infinite; Totaro gave further examples (Chow groups mod 2).
'Groupe libre de type fini?' for A_τ: the answer is no in general. Clemens (1983) showed the Griffiths group can have infinite rank. A_num is free of finite type, which was known.

'V.A.?': an abelian-variety kernel exists for divisors and for 0-cycles (Albanese), but not in general. Mumford (1969) showed infinite-dimensionality for 0-cycles; in general only an algebraic representative of the algebraically trivial part exists, in codimension 2 (Murre).

missed.claim: Grothendieck places the torsion part of cycles modulo algebraic equivalence ('groupe fini?') and the abelian-variety nature of the continuous part ('V.A.?') in a single diagram with the K-theoretic filtrations. This makes the torsion questions part of his standard-conjecture programme around 1968–71. Both questions were later answered (Schoen/Totaro; Mumford/Murre), but this early explicit formulation by Grothendieck is not usually cited.
missed.quote: Groupe fini ? ... V.A.? ... flèches qui sont des isomorphismes de torsion
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents that Grothendieck asked integral and torsion questions about algebraic equivalence, not only rational ones.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear overview diagram of standard notions and well-known open questions of the late 1960s. Its interest is mainly historical (integral and torsion questions, the K-theory link). There are no new results.
transcription_corrections: 'A_Z' is probably A_τ (τ-equivalence: algebraic equivalence modulo torsion); the arrow label '? Z' to A_num is probably '⊗Q ≃?' or similar.
The right-hand duplicate column is crossed out and should not be read as part of the diagram.
The circled 'HC' may be 'AH' (Atiyah–Hirzebruch); 'car. 0' may read 'C-ex.?' (contre-exemple). The phrase is 'au moins en théorie transcendante'.
The arrows inside the 'théorie continue' box are marked '?', with labels uncertain ('≃?' rather than 'Z').
A dashed arrow with '?' from G_top K to A_{Z_ℓ-hom} is omitted in the transcription.
Bottom right: likely 'Autres équivalences : l'équivalence algébrique r[?] et les équivalences de Weil[?] wh et W définies par Lieberman'.
